_synthetic: Invented cases for a timed triage drill. Gold colours are hand-computed from the SATS 2012 adult chart; a clinician should re-check them before use with staff.

vignettes.text: 34-year-old man, walked in. Headache 3 days. RR 16, HR 88, BP 124/80, T 37.2, alert, no injury.
58-year-old woman, came in with help. Breathless since this morning. RR 26, HR 114, BP 150/90, T 37.0, alert, no injury. SpO2 not measured.
25-year-old woman, 24 weeks pregnant, walked in. Small PV bleed this morning, now stopped. RR 18, HR 92, BP 110/70, T 36.8, alert.
70-year-old man on a stretcher. Family says he became confused today. RR 24, HR 124, BP 92/60, T 38.9, responds to voice.
19-year-old man, walked in. Cut on left hand from a knife 2 hours ago, bleeding controlled with a bandage. RR 16, HR 96, BP 128/76, T 36.9, alert.
45-year-old woman, walked in. Chest pain for 40 minutes. RR 18, HR 90, BP 140/90, T 36.6, alert.
62-year-old man, known diabetic, walked in. Feels unwell. Glucotest 2.4 mmol/L. RR 18, HR 102, BP 130/80, T 36.5, alert but sweaty.
30-year-old woman, walked in. Burning on urination 3 days. RR 14, HR 80, BP 118/72, T 37.4, alert.
40-year-old man, walked in with help. Vomiting since yesterday, cannot keep fluids down. RR 20, HR 118, BP 96/60, T 37.9, alert.
52-year-old woman, walked in. Cough for 2 months, on TB treatment. RR 22, HR 98, BP 112/70, T 37.6, alert. SpO2 95%.
